summary: Owned units s0045–s0066 are Wang Xizhi’s counsel after a northern defeat and contain no births, deaths, or ages. Chen Sheng and Wu Guang appear only in the proverbial 勝廣之憂; Jin Shu 80 does not date their rising, so BC 209 is an imported Shiji year applied to a later Qin-rebellion allusion and cannot stand as their own event or as an active hint. Yao and Shun are explicitly 古人 / 往代 exemplars, so legendary antiquity is supported. The letter 又與會稽王箋, and Wang’s 今 / 當今 in that letter, belong to the Prince of Kuaiji as addressee and to Wang as author: the same cluster already has 今軍破於外 while 殷浩、荀羨 are still to be recalled. Jin Shu 8 and Zizhi Tongjian place Hao’s Yao Xiang defeat in winter Yonghe 9 and his dismissal in Yonghe 10/II; conventional Eastern-Jin 永和九年–十年 are AD 353–354, and the Chinese year itself straddles those Western years, so the 353–354 window is uncertainty about one letter, not a dynasty span. Wang’s 353–355 hint matches that letter plus the later famine window and the Yonghe 9 Lanting context.

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi’s later allusion to a Chen Sheng–Wu Guang-style uprising, not Chen Sheng’s own dated rising.
itemChecks.reason: The dated event belongs to Wang Xizhi’s present-tense warning in the letter to Yin Hao, not to Chen Sheng. s0057 only fears a Sheng-Guang-type revolt after likening current exactions to Qin; it gives no Qin Er Shi year, month, or narrative of the Dazexiang rising. BC 209 is therefore not converted from this passage. A later biography may attest an earlier life event, but a typological 勝廣之憂 is reception, not that attestation. The year must not be used as Chen Sheng’s life date.

evidence.quote: 殆同秦政，惟未加參夷之刑耳，恐勝廣之憂，無復日矣。

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi’s later allusion to a Chen Sheng–Wu Guang-style uprising, not Wu Guang’s own dated rising.
itemChecks.reason: Wu Guang is coupled with Chen Sheng only as the second half of 勝廣之憂. The owner of the dated speech is Wang Xizhi warning that present Jin exactions may provoke a Qin-style revolt; Wu Guang himself has no event, year, or age in the owned units. BC 209 is not in the Chinese and cannot be read out of the two-character tag 勝廣.

evidence.quote: 恐勝廣之憂，無復日矣。

itemChecks.event: The Prince of Kuaiji is addressed in Wang Xizhi’s letter arguing that Yin Hao must not launch another northern campaign.
itemChecks.reason: The event owner is the living addressee 會稽王 of the 箋, not a later commemoration. s0058 places that letter immediately after the Hao letter that already says 今軍破於外, and the same 箋 still treats Hao as a commander who can be recalled (s0074 令殷浩、荀羨還據合肥、廣陵). Jin Shu 8 dates Hao’s Yao Xiang defeat to winter Yonghe 9 and his dismissal to Yonghe 10/II; Zizhi Tongjian labels those years 癸丑 AD 353 and 甲寅 AD 354. The letter can still fall in AD 353 after the tenth-month defeat, so the start is onOrAfter 353, not after 353. The 353–354 interval is uncertainty about this one letter, not activity across a dynasty. Conventional 永和九年 is not a Gregorian day date; the Chinese year itself runs from early 353 into early 354.

itemChecks.reason: 殿下 in s0074 is the same 會稽王 as s0058; the dated act is the Prince being asked to change present policy, not a descendant’s later honor. 今 / 當今 mark the letter’s present (今 is in the same 箋 at s0061; s0074 has 當今). Endpoints follow the same Hao-defeat / Hao-still-in-command window as claim-176: after Yonghe 9 winter (AD 353) and before Yonghe 10/II dismissal (AD 354). Do not collapse the window to a single year.

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi writes the letter to the Prince of Kuaiji on present policy after Hao’s defeat.
itemChecks.reason: Wang is the author of the 箋 that begins at s0058 and continues through s0074; 今 / 當今 date his writing, not a later reception of Wang. The same post-defeat, pre-dismissal bounds as claim-176 give AD 353–354 for this one letter. Context items then add the Yonghe 9 Lanting gathering (s0115) and a later famine window; those do not contradict 353–354 for this letter and explain why the person hint runs to 355.

personChecks.reason: Chen Sheng’s only supplied items are claim-174 and hints-p019, both built on s0057 勝廣之憂. That sentence is Wang’s fear of a future Qin-style revolt, not Chen Sheng’s rising, death, or age. No owned unit dates him. Assigning BC 209 as attestation and as an active hint makes a later allusion look like his own dated event. Keep the mention as retrospective reception dated to the letter’s present; do not certify a life year from this chapter alone.

Context claim-215 dates 時東土饑荒 and granary relief on a wider 353–355 window after the letter cluster in the narrative. hints-p028’s AD 353–355 is that union, not a posthumous honor used as a life date. Owned units s0045–s0066 have no 年、卒、生 for Wang; the later 年五十九卒 and 永和十一年 oath lie outside this slice and were not treated as missing here. No contradiction among the supplied items.

findings.problem: s0057 恐勝廣之憂 is Wang Xizhi’s present-tense fear of a Qin-style revolt. It does not date Chen Sheng’s or Wu Guang’s rising, death, or age. BC 209 is imported from the Shiji 二世元年 July narrative, then reused as their attestation year and as active hints, turning later reception into living activity.
findings.action: Keep the mention. Recast claim-174 and claim-175 as retrospective-reference (or attestation with receptionType retrospective) whose date is the Hao-letter present, sharing the 353–354 letter window or remaining unresolved with a reason that Jin Shu 80 gives no Sheng-Guang year. Remove westernYear BC 209. Clear hints-p019 and hints-p020 of BC 209; do not invent a life year or delete the persons.
